editorial:
Imagine landing your dream job at a company that feels like a golden ticket. That is exactly what happens to Brian, a young guy who gets swept up in the wild world of Enron. You will see him go from a nervous new hire to someone living the high life, spending money he does not really have and partying with corporate bosses. The vibe is a mix of high-energy greed and total chaos. It feels like a cautionary tale about what happens when everyone decides to cheat the system just to look successful on paper.

What really works here is how the movie shows the slow slide from confidence to complete panic. The acting makes you feel Brian's stress as the walls close in. While some parts feel a bit like an old TV movie, the story is still a wild ride. You should definitely check this out if you like stories about big scams and corporate lies. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for it on streaming or grab a digital rental on Apple TV to see the fallout in the best quality possible.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when Enron goes bankrupt and the stock price hits zero. You see Brian realize that the bosses lied to everyone while they saved their own money. The movie ends with the company collapsing and the employees losing their life savings. Brian is left with nothing but a hard lesson about greed. It wraps up by showing that the big players got away with a lot while the little guys lost everything.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true stories about big scams and business failures.
